title: Unified Migration Orchestration for Global Retailers
business: A multinational retail enterprise managing a fragmented portfolio of legacy on-premises data centers and disparate cloud-native microservices.
problem: The IT operations team struggles with visibility, as they lack a centralized dashboard to track the progress of hundreds of individual application migrations occurring across different AWS regions and third-party partner tools.
solution: AWS Migration Hub serves as the central control plane, aggregating status updates from AWS Application Discovery Service and AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) into a single, unified view to track migration progress across the entire portfolio.
steps: Enable AWS Migration Hub in the home region to serve as the central repository for migration data.
Deploy AWS Application Discovery Service agents on-premises to map existing dependencies and server configurations.
Integrate third-party migration tools with the Migration Hub API to push status updates into the central dashboard.
Configure AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) to automate the replication of source servers into the target AWS environment.
Monitor the unified status dashboard to identify bottlenecks in the migration lifecycle across all integrated tools.
outcome: The organization achieves a consolidated view of migration status, enabling stakeholders to make informed decisions and synchronize cutover activities across geographically dispersed teams.
limitation: Migration Hub acts as a tracking and orchestration layer rather than a data migration engine; it relies on the accuracy of status reporting from integrated tools. To verify data integrity, administrators must manually reconcile the status in the Hub against the source tool logs.

questions.question: In Unified Migration Orchestration for Global Retailers, what is the primary function of the Migration Hub?
options: Aggregating status updates from various migration tools into a unified view
Automatically converting legacy code into cloud-native microservices
Providing physical hardware for on-premises data center expansion
Managing the billing and procurement of third-party SaaS applications
questions.explanation: The solution describes the Hub as a central control plane that aggregates status updates from various services.
questions.evidence: AWS Migration Hub serves as the central control plane, aggregating status updates from AWS Application Discovery Service and AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) into a single, unified view to track migration progress across the entire portfolio.

questions.question: In Unified Migration Orchestration for Global Retailers, what is a key limitation of the Migration Hub?
options: It cannot track migrations across multiple AWS regions
It is a tracking layer and does not perform the actual data migration itself
It requires all migration tools to be built by AWS
It cannot integrate with third-party partner tools
questions.explanation: The limitation section clarifies that the Hub tracks progress but relies on other tools for the actual migration work.
